subject: SLA amendment: monthly credit ceiling and latency tiers
messages:
From: Emily Harris <emily.harris@skyforge.io>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: SkyForge Ops <ops@skyforge.io>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SLA amendment request — monthly credit ceiling + latency tiers

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the booth demo last week — Cliff and the engineering team found the Redwood runtime impressive. As we move from POC to production, procurement has asked us to get a tighter SLA template in place for our Standard plan workloads. Two asks from our side: 

1) Monthly service credit ceiling: because SkyForge guarantees a strong uptime for our end customers, procurement is requesting the monthly remediation cap be increased above the standard 4% floor. They want a mechanism that scales with severity and total invoice (we suggested an initial ceiling in the RFP, but Redwood's template is lower).

2) Latency-tier carveouts: our workloads are bursty — we care about 95th and 99th percentile tail latency windows. We need the SLA to include latency bands with corresponding credits (e.g., if 95p > 600ms for X hours).

Attached: June latency sample (latency-report-June.csv). Can you share how Redwood typically computes monthly caps (percentage of invoice vs fixed-dollar), and whether you can accommodate a latency-tier table?

Goal: finalize an amendment for our legal team by Friday, 10 July.

Thanks,
Emily Harris
Head of Platform SRE, SkyForge

Attachments: latency-report-June.csv (CSV, 48KB)
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Emily Harris <emily.harris@skyforge.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request — monthly credit ceiling + latency tiers

Emily —

Appreciate the clear asks and the sample latency export. Quick answers up front: we can support a percentage-based monthly cap tied to invoice, and we can add a latency-tier table to the amendment, but we need to align on formulas and risk allocation. 

A couple of clarifying questions before we draft the amendment:
- Is SkyForge asking for the monthly cap to be a hard percentage of MRC (monthly recurring charge) or a dollar cap? (we support both; percentage is easier to compute for multi-product invoices)
- For latency tiers, do you want credits triggered by sustained tail latency (e.g., more than N consecutive 5-minute windows) or by aggregate monthly windows?

Internally looping in Ben and Marissa to propose internal guardrails. We're prioritizing getting you a redline version quickly so legal has something to react to.

I'll draft a first-pass amendment and attach a PDF for review.

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed approach — monthly credit ceiling & latency tiers

Folks — following Chloe's note, here is a concise proposal we can send to SkyForge as an internal first-pass (I've kept the language direct so legal can redline).

1) Monthly credit ceiling (proposed):
- Credit calculation: for an uptime or latency breach, remediation = (service-level-deficit % * monthly_invoice).
- Monthly cap: remediation credits per month capped at the lesser of (a) 8% of the monthly invoice, or (b) $150,000.
- Rationale: percentage ties to economic exposure, fixed dollar avoids runaway credits on very large invoices.

2) Latency tiers (proposed):
- Define two latency Service Levels: 95th percentile and 99th percentile measured on per-region aggregated traffic.
- Trigger rule: a latency-band credit is triggered if the 5-minute rolling 95p or 99p exceeds the threshold for more than three non-overlapping 5-minute windows within a 24-hour period.
- Credit mapping example (monthly):
  - 95p > 600ms but <= 1000ms: 0.5% of monthly invoice per qualified incident (up to monthly cap)
  - 95p > 1000ms: 1.5% of monthly invoice per qualified incident
  - 99p > 1200ms: 3% of monthly invoice per qualified incident

3) Maintenance carveouts & reporting
- Scheduled maintenance with 48-hr notice is excluded. Emergency maintenance limited to documented emergency playbook.
- Redwood will provide a latency telemetry export (CSV) and an incident timeline for any claimed credit.

If this is acceptable, I'll create a PDF amendment and include the exact formula with a worked example using SkyForge's expected MRC. Chloe — if you want to soften the cap (e.g., 6% instead of 8%) to move negotiations, say so and I'll update.

-ben

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Emily Harris <emily.harris@skyforge.io>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: SkyForge Ops <ops@skyforge.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed approach — monthly credit ceiling & latency tiers

Chloe/Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the worked examples. From procurement's perspective the 8%/ $150k ceiling is a lot closer to what we need, but given SkyForge's vertical (real-time payments) and contractual exposure to our own customers, procurement is going to push for a higher safety net: a monthly cap of up to 12% for production-critical routes for the first 6 months post-cutover.

On latency tiers: the trigger rule with three non-overlapping 5-minute windows is fine, but we also need an aggregate monthly bucket for intermittent tail spikes (e.g., if there are 20 short spikes each <3 minutes, we want a separate aggregated credit after threshold Y). Can Redwood provide both per-incident credits and a monthly aggregated tail-spike credit?

We understand maintenance carveouts, but for the first 90 days we want one maintenance blackout (i.e., no scheduled maintenance on critical routes) or a credit equal to twice the normal latency credit if we’re notified <24 hours in advance.

If you can send a redline amendment that supports: (a) production-critical route cap up to 12% for first 6 months, (b) per-incident + monthly aggregate tail bucket, and (c) one 90-day maintenance blackout protection, we can escalate to SkyForge legal immediately.

Emily
Head of Platform SRE, SkyForge
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Emily Harris <emily.harris@skyforge.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jul 2025 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request — monthly credit ceiling + latency tiers (draft attached)

Emily —

Thanks, and good points. We've digested SkyForge's asks and Ben and I iterated on a draft. Attached is SLA-Amendment-draft-v1.pdf with three callouts that reflect your asks:

1) Production-critical route exception: a temporary increased monthly cap provision that can be enabled for up to 6 months post-go-live. The draft sets the upper bound at 12% of MRC for enabled routes; activation requires a signed schedule identifying the routes.

2) Per-incident and monthly aggregate latency credits: we've included both mechanisms. The monthly aggregate bucket triggers if the count of qualifying 5-minute tail windows exceeds a monthly threshold (worked example included).

3) 90-day maintenance blackout: draft includes a single blackout window for specified critical routes; if Redwood schedules maintenance during that window without 24-hr notice, the credit multiplier is 2x for any latency credit awarded.

Next steps: Ben will convert the draft to a legal redline (target EOD Thu). If SkyForge confirms the activation mechanism for production-critical routes (list of routes + effective date), we'll push legal + DocuSign.

Attaching: SLA-Amendment-draft-v1.pdf (PDF, 12 pages). Also uploaded the latency CSV you provided to the shared drive and linked in HubSpot.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
